prompt: why do websites not store your actual password
reply: Because a stolen database should not hand over your login. Sites store a hash instead: a one-way scramble that is easy to run forwards and impractical to run backwards. When you sign in they hash what you typed and compare scrambles, never the password itself — which is why a real site can reset your password but can never tell you the old one. 🔐 Good sites pick a deliberately slow hash too, so guessing millions of passwords stays expensive. [CHIPS]What is a hash|Why salting helps|Spot a bad site[/CHIPS]

prompt: how does a game run at 60 frames per second

So optimising a game is really deadline management. [CHIPS]What drops frames|Why 60 not 30|Show the loop[/CHIPS]

[CHIPS]What is log n|Show an example|What is n squared[/CHIPS]
